===mlflow.toml===
# MLflow channel for television (tv).
# Browse experiments, runs, and registered models against any MLflow tracking
# backend (file:./mlruns, sqlite:///path/to/mlflow.db, or http://server:port).
#
# Usage:
#   tv mlflow
#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://192.168.222.207:15002 tv mlflow
#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
#
# Prerequisites:
#   - `mlflow` installed (provided by dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools — the
#     CLI binary is what we exec under the `uv run --script` shebang of the
#     two helpers).
#   - `uv` on PATH (installed by uv role; required to resolve the PEP 723
#     inline-deps block in mlflow-source.py / mlflow-preview.py).
#
# Backend mode is resolved entirely from $MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI. When unset,
# mlflow 3.12+ auto-detects from $PWD: an `mlflow.db` file picks sqlite, an
# `mlruns/` dir picks file mode, otherwise it creates `mlruns/`. To pin a
# backend at launch time:
#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http://host:port tv mlflow
#   MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=sqlite:///$PWD/mlflow.db tv mlflow
#
# Source cycling (Ctrl+S):
#   1. Experiments     all active experiments
#   2. Recent runs     top 50 runs across all experiments, by start_time desc
#   3. Runs (scoped)   runs in $MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID (hint row when unset;
#                      Alt+R on an experiment row sets it and re-launches tv)
#   4. Models          registered models from the model registry
#
# Preview cycling (Ctrl+F):
#   1. Full JSON       params, metrics, tags, artifact_uri, timestamps
#   2. Metrics-only    sorted key=value table; or aggregated across recent
#                      runs for an experiment row
#
# Keybindings:
#   Enter      Context-aware:
#                experiment row -> re-launch tv scoped to that experiment's
#                                  runs (nested drill-in; Esc exits the
#                                  drilled view back to the shell)
#                run / model row -> open full JSON detail in pager
#   Ctrl+Y     Copy id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard
#   Ctrl+O     Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only; prints a hint
#              otherwise)
#   Ctrl+B     Same as Ctrl+O — "B for browser" muscle-memory alias
#   Alt+R      Explicit drill — same as Enter on an experiment row,
#              available as a backup binding for muscle memory
#   Alt+J      Dump full JSON to terminal (paged)
#   Ctrl+F     Cycle preview
#   Ctrl+S     Cycle source
#
# No `watch` field: mlflow imports are heavy (~1s warm, several seconds cold);
# experiments and runs change on the minute scale anyway. Press Ctrl+R to
# refresh manually after logging a new run.
#
# Hint row sentinel: when the backend is unreachable or a source is unscoped,
# the helper emits a single row with id `__hint__`. Real mlflow ids never
# collide (experiment_ids are non-negative ints; run_ids are 32-hex; model
# names cannot contain `__hint__` in practice).

[metadata]
name = "mlflow"
description = "MLflow tracking: experiments, runs, registered models (file/sqlite/http backends)"
requirements = ["mlflow", "uv"]

[source]
command = [
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py experiments",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-recent",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py models",
]
display = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:2}  {split:\\t:3}  ({split:\\t:4})"
output = "{split:\\t:0}"
no_sort = true

[preview]
# Helper always emits valid JSON now; pipe through `bat -l json` so the
# preview pane gets syntax highlighting (numbers, strings, keys). Same
# trick super-productivity.toml plays with `jq -C`, but bat's truecolor
# theme is easier on the eyes for nested objects.
#
# `--paging=never` is load-bearing: bat detects "not a TTY" inside TV's
# preview pipe and would otherwise still buffer; we want streamed output.
# `--plain` strips line numbers / decorations so the preview pane shows
# only the rendered content.
command = [
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full    | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
  "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view metrics | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json",
]
header = "{split:\\t:1}  {split:\\t:3}"

[ui]
input_header = "MLflow"

[ui.preview_panel]
size = 60

[keybindings]
enter = "actions:open-or-drill"
# Override TV's default ctrl-y (which copies the entire display row) with
# id-only copy. Matches super-productivity.toml's convention.
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-id"
ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"
# Ctrl+B is the muscle-memory alias — same action body as Ctrl+O. Reusing
# the existing action keeps the channel self-contained even if `mlf` (the
# umbrella CLI in dot_dotfiles/bin/) isn't installed.
ctrl-b = "actions:open-browser"
alt-r = "actions:drill-runs"
alt-j = "actions:dump-json"

[actions.open-or-drill]
description = "Drill into experiment runs (experiment row) / open JSON detail (others)"
# Kind detection mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
#   __hint__       -> show the help JSON (helpful when MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI is
#                     misconfigured: lets the user read the example URIs)
#   digit-only id  -> drill: re-exec tv with MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID + a
#                     --source-command override so the nested view shows ONLY
#                     this experiment's runs. Esc exits the drill back to
#                     the shell (TV does not have a back-stack; rerun
#                     `tv mlflow` for cross-experiment views).
#   anything else  -> open JSON detail in pager
#
# The header is set to "MLflow / <exp_name>" inside the drilled view so it's
# obvious you're in the nested context, not the top-level one. {split:\t:3}
# carries the experiment name in the experiments source layout (cols are:
# id, marker, lifecycle, name, last_update).
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
  __hint__) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
  *[!0-9]*) ~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto "$id" --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _ ;;
  *) MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" ;;
esac"""
mode = "execute"

[actions.copy-id]
description = "Copy row id (experiment_id / run_id / model_name) to clipboard"
command = """_clip() { local d; d=$(cat); [ -z "$d" ] && return; if command -v pbcopy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | pbcopy; elif command -v wl-copy >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | wl-copy; elif command -v xclip >/dev/null; then printf '%s' "$d" | xclip -selection clipboard; else printf '%b' "\\033]52;c;$(printf '%s' "$d" | base64)\\007" > /dev/tty; fi; }; printf '%s' '{split:\\t:0}' | _clip"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.open-browser]
description = "Open in browser (HTTP tracking URI only)"
# Build the URL inside the action so we read the live env var rather than
# baking it in. Inference mirrors mlflow-preview.py's _detect_kind:
#   32-hex id -> need a roundtrip to find experiment_id, just open root
#   all-digit -> /#/experiments/<id>
#   else      -> /#/models/<name>
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; uri="${MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI:-}"; case "$uri" in http://*|https://*) ;; *) printf '[open-browser] needs MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI=http(s)://… — current: %s\\n' "${uri:-(unset)}"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; case "$id" in __hint__) printf '[open-browser] no row selected\\n'; sleep 2; exit 0 ;; esac; url="$uri/"; if [ "${#id}" = "32" ] && printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9a-f]{32}$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/0/runs/$id"; elif printf '%s' "$id" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+$'; then url="$uri/#/experiments/$id"; else url="$uri/#/models/$id"; fi; if command -v open >/dev/null; then open "$url"; elif command -v xdg-open >/dev/null; then xdg-open "$url" >/dev/null 2>&1 & elif command -v wslview >/dev/null; then wslview "$url"; else printf '[open-browser] no opener (open/xdg-open/wslview) — URL was: %s\\n' "$url"; sleep 2; fi"""
mode = "fork"

[actions.drill-runs]
description = "Re-launch tv scoped to the highlighted experiment (Alt+R)"
# Same payload as the Enter drill branch — explicit binding for muscle
# memory and discoverability. No-op + hint on non-experiment rows so the
# user doesn't accidentally drill into an empty unscoped view.
command = """id='{split:\\t:0}'; name='{split:\\t:3}'; case "$id" in
  __hint__|*[!0-9]*) printf '[drill-runs] not an experiment row (id=%s). Move to the Experiments source (Ctrl+S) and try again.\\n' "$id"; sleep 2; exit 0 ;;
esac
MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID="$id" tv mlflow --source-command "~/.config/television/mlflow-source.py runs-experiment" --input-header "MLflow / $name" """
mode = "execute"

[actions.dump-json]
description = "Print full JSON detail to terminal, paged"
command = "~/.config/television/mlflow-preview.py auto '{split:\\t:0}' --view full | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=json | less -R; echo; echo '[Press Enter to exit]'; read -r _"
mode = "execute"
```

39	def make_client() -> "MlflowClient":
40	    """Build a MlflowClient. Imports lazily; silences mlflow's INFO logs.
41	
42	    `logging.getLogger("mlflow").setLevel(WARNING)` MUST run AFTER
43	    `import mlflow` — mlflow.utils.logging_utils installs handlers at
44	    import time and pre-import setLevel calls get overwritten.

46	    import logging
47	
48	    # `from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient` loads the top-level mlflow
49	    # package as a side-effect, which is when mlflow.utils.logging_utils
50	    # installs its INFO-level handlers. The setLevel call below MUST run
51	    # after that, not before — pre-import setLevel gets overwritten.
52	    from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient
53	
54	    logging.getLogger("mlflow").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
55	    logging.getLogger("alembic").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
56	    return MlflowClient()

59	def detect_kind(ident: str) -> str:

62	    Returns one of: "run" | "experiment" | "model".

64	      32-hex     -> run        (RUN_ID_RE)
65	      digits-only-> experiment (mlflow assigns non-negative ints)
66	      else       -> model      (registered model name; arbitrary string)
67	
68	    Kept in sync with dot_config/television/executable_mlflow-preview.py:_detect_kind.
69	    """
70	    if RUN_ID_RE.match(ident):
71	        return "run"
72	    if ident.isdigit():
73	        return "experiment"
74	    return "model"

77	def ms_to_iso(ms: int | None) -> str:
78	    """Convert mlflow's millisecond timestamps to local ISO strings.
79	
80	    Returns "-" on missing/invalid input so table renderers can use the
81	    output directly without further None-checks.
82	    """
83	    if not ms:
84	        return "-"

86	        dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ms) / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).astimezone()
87	        return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")

156	def copy_id(payload: str) -> int:

158	
159	    Provider chain: pbcopy → wl-copy → xclip → OSC 52 fallback to /dev/tty.
160	    Mirrors the shell snippet in mlflow.toml [actions.copy-id]. Pure helper
161	    so the TUI's `y` action can reuse it without spawning a subprocess.
162	    """
163	    providers = [
164	        ["pbcopy"],
165	        ["wl-copy"],
166	        ["xclip", "-selection", "clipboard"],
167	    ]
168	    for cmd in providers:
169	        if shutil.which(cmd[0]):
170	            try:
171	                subprocess.run(cmd, input=payload, text=True, check=True)
172	            except subprocess.CalledProcessError as e:
173	                print(
174	                    f"mlf copy: {cmd[0]} failed ({e.returncode}); falling through",
175	                    file=sys.stderr,
176	                )

178	            print(

180	                file=sys.stderr,
181	            )
182	            return 0
183	
184	    try:
185	        import base64

187	        b64 = base64.b64encode(payload.encode()).decode()
188	        with open("/dev/tty", "w") as tty:
189	            tty.write(f"\033]52;c;{b64}\007")
190	        print(

193	        )
194	        return 0
195	    except OSError as e:
196	        print(

198	            "  Install pbcopy/wl-copy/xclip, or run inside a TTY that supports OSC 52.",
199	            file=sys.stderr,

204	def fetch_histories(
205	    client: "MlflowClient",
206	    run_id: str,
207	    keys: list[str],
208	) -> tuple[dict[str, tuple[list[int], list[float]]], list[tuple[str, str]]]:
209	    """Fetch metric history for every key. Skip-on-error per key.
210	
211	    Returns (series, skipped) where:
212	      series  = {key: (steps_sorted, values_aligned), ...}
213	      skipped = [(key, "ExceptionType: message"), ...]
214	
215	    One slow / broken key (commonly a `system.*` metric over a flaky link)
216	    shouldn't abort the whole batch — both the CLI `mlf plot` and the TUI
217	    Plot tab surface skipped keys in a separate warning instead. Bump
218	    MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT for the whole invocation if a host needs
219	    longer per-key reads.
220	    """
221	    series: dict[str, tuple[list[int], list[float]]] = {}
222	    skipped: list[tuple[str, str]] = []
223	    for key in keys:
224	        try:
225	            history = client.get_metric_history(run_id, key)
226	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
227	            skipped.append((key, f"{type(e).__name__}: {str(e).splitlines()[0][:80]}"))
228	            continue
229	        if not history:
230	            continue
231	        sorted_hist = sorted(history, key=lambda m: m.step)
232	        steps = [m.step for m in sorted_hist]
233	        values = [m.value for m in sorted_hist]
234	        series[key] = (steps, values)
235	    return series, skipped

59	@dataclass
60	class Row:
61	    id: str
62	    kind: str
63	    name: str
64	    status: str
65	    lifecycle: str
66	    extra: str
67	    last_update: str
68	
69	
70	def _experiments(client, limit: int) -> list[Row]:
71	    rows = []
72	    for e in client.search_experiments(max_results=limit):
73	        rows.append(
74	            Row(
75	                id=str(e.experiment_id),
76	                kind="experiment",
77	                name=e.name or "(unnamed)",
78	                status="-",
79	                lifecycle=e.lifecycle_stage or "-",
80	                extra=e.artifact_location or "",
81	                last_update=ms_to_iso(e.last_update_time),
82	            )
83	        )
84	    return rows
85	
86	
87	def _runs(client, limit: int, exp_id: str | None) -> list[Row]:
88	    if exp_id:
89	        try:
90	            exp = client.get_experiment(exp_id)
91	        except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
92	            print(
93	                f"mlf list: experiment_id={exp_id} not found — {str(e)[:80]}",
94	                file=sys.stderr,
95	            )
96	            return []
97	        exp_ids = [exp.experiment_id]
98	        name_by_id = {exp.experiment_id: (exp.name or "(unnamed)")}
99	    else:
100	        exps = list(client.search_experiments(max_results=200))
101	        if not exps:
102	            return []
103	        exp_ids = [e.experiment_id for e in exps]
104	        name_by_id = {e.experiment_id: (e.name or "(unnamed)") for e in exps}
105	    runs = client.search_runs(
106	        experiment_ids=exp_ids,
107	        max_results=limit,
108	        order_by=["attributes.start_time DESC"],
109	    )
110	    rows = []
111	    for r in runs:
112	        info = r.info
113	        rows.append(
114	            Row(
115	                id=info.run_id,
116	                kind="run",
117	                name=info.run_name or info.run_id[:8],
118	                status=STATUS_ICON.get(info.status, info.status or "?"),
119	                lifecycle=info.lifecycle_stage or "-",
120	                extra=name_by_id.get(info.experiment_id, info.experiment_id),
121	                last_update=ms_to_iso(info.start_time),
122	            )
123	        )
124	    return rows
125	
126	
127	def _models(client, limit: int) -> list[Row]:
128	    try:
129	        models = list(client.search_registered_models(max_results=limit))
130	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
131	        # The file: backend has no registry — surface a friendly hint
132	        # instead of a raw traceback.
133	        print(
134	            f"mlf list models: registry unavailable — {str(e)[:200]}\n"
135	            f"  tracking_uri: {tracking_uri()}",
136	            file=sys.stderr,
137	        )
138	        return []
139	    rows = []
140	    for m in models:
141	        stages = sorted({v.current_stage for v in (m.latest_versions or []) if v.current_stage})
142	        stage_label = ",".join(stages) if stages else "-"
143	        rows.append(
144	            Row(
145	                id=m.name,
146	                kind="model",
147	                name=m.name,
148	                status=stage_label,
149	                lifecycle="-",
150	                extra=(m.description or "").splitlines()[0] if m.description else "",
151	                last_update=ms_to_iso(m.last_updated_timestamp),
152	            )
153	        )
154	    return rows
155	
156	
157	_COLUMNS_BY_KIND = {
158	    "experiments": [("id", "id"), ("lifecycle", "lifecycle"), ("name", "name"), ("last_update", "last_update")],
159	    "runs": [
160	        ("id", "run_id"),
161	        ("status", "status"),
162	        ("extra", "experiment"),
163	        ("name", "run_name"),
164	        ("last_update", "start_time"),
165	    ],
166	    "models": [
167	        ("id", "name"),
168	        ("status", "stages"),
169	        ("extra", "description"),
170	        ("last_update", "last_update"),
171	    ],
172	}
173	
174	
175	def _render_table(kind: str, rows: list[Row]) -> None:
176	    table = Table(show_lines=False, header_style="bold")
177	    cols = _COLUMNS_BY_KIND[kind]
178	    for _, header in cols:
179	        table.add_column(header)
180	    for row in rows:
181	        table.add_row(*[getattr(row, attr) for attr, _ in cols])
182	    Console().print(table)
183	
184	
185	def cli(args: Args) -> int:
186	    client = make_client()
187	    if args.kind == "experiments":
188	        rows = _experiments(client, args.limit)
189	    elif args.kind == "runs":
190	        rows = _runs(client, args.limit, args.experiment)
191	    else:
192	        rows = _models(client, args.limit)
193	
194	    if args.json_out:
195	        print(json.dumps([dataclasses.asdict(r) for r in rows], indent=2, default=str))
196	        return 0
197	
198	    if not rows:
199	        print(f"mlf list {args.kind}: (no rows)", file=sys.stderr)
200	        return 0
201	
202	    _render_table(args.kind, rows)
203	    return 0
204	
205	
206	def main() -> int:
207	    return cli(tyro.cli(Args, prog="mlf list"))
208	
209	
210	if __name__ == "__main__":
211	    sys.exit(main())
212
```
</details></tool-use>

1	#!/usr/bin/env -S uv run --script
2	# /// script
3	# requires-python = ">=3.11"
4	# dependencies = ["mlflow>=3.4"]
5	# ///
6	"""Source emitter for the `mlflow` tv channel.
7	
8	Usage:
9	    mlflow-source.py <experiments|runs-recent|runs-experiment|models>
10	
11	Emits TSV rows. Column 0 is always the id that TV passes to the preview
12	command (experiment_id / run_id / model_name). Column 1 is an emoji or
13	status marker; remaining columns are display-only.
14	
15	Backend resolution honours `MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI` (env var). When unset,
16	mlflow falls back to `file:./mlruns` in the current directory.
17	
18	On any unreachable / unconfigured backend, a single hint row with id `0`
19	is emitted instead of crashing — preserves the same UX as the
20	super-productivity channel.
21	"""
22	from __future__ import annotations
23	
24	import os
25	import sys
26	import warnings
27	from datetime import datetime, timezone
28	from typing import Iterable
29	
30	os.environ.setdefault("PYTHONWARNINGS", "ignore")
31	# Fail fast on unreachable HTTP tracking servers: stale DNS or a typo'd
32	# MLFLOW_TRACKING_URI would otherwise hang TV for ~60s before the exception
33	# handler emits the hint row (mlflow defaults are 120s / 5 retries).
34	os.environ.setdefault("MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_TIMEOUT", "5")
35	os.environ.setdefault("MLFLOW_HTTP_REQUEST_MAX_RETRIES", "1")
36	warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")
37	
38	import logging  # noqa: E402
39	import mlflow  # noqa: E402
40	from mlflow.tracking import MlflowClient  # noqa: E402
41	
42	# Silence mlflow's own INFO logging (e.g. "Creating initial MLflow database
43	# tables..." when sqlite is auto-bootstrapped). MUST run AFTER `import
44	# mlflow`: mlflow.utils.logging_utils installs its handlers at import time
45	# and pre-import setLevel calls get overwritten.
46	logging.getLogger("mlflow").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
47	logging.getLogger("alembic").setLevel(logging.WARNING)
48	
49	MAX_EXPERIMENTS = 200
50	MAX_RUNS = 50
51	
52	STATUS_ICON = {
53	    "RUNNING": "▶ running",
54	    "FINISHED": "✓ done",
55	    "FAILED": "✗ failed",
56	    "KILLED": "■ killed",
57	    "SCHEDULED": "○ scheduled",
58	}
59	
60	
61	def _clean(value: object) -> str:
62	    s = "" if value is None else str(value)
63	    return s.replace("\t", " ").replace("\n", " ").replace("\r", " ")
64	
65	
66	def tsv(*cols: object) -> None:
67	    print("\t".join(_clean(c) for c in cols))
68	
69	
70	def _ms_to_iso(ms: int | None) -> str:
71	    if not ms:
72	        return "-"
73	    try:
74	        dt = datetime.fromtimestamp(int(ms) / 1000, tz=timezone.utc).astimezone()
75	        return dt.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M")
76	    except (OverflowError, OSError, ValueError):
77	        return "-"
78	
79	
80	def _hint(reason: str, detail: str) -> None:
81	    # Sentinel id `__hint__` MUST NOT collide with real mlflow ids — mlflow's
82	    # default backend assigns experiment_id `0` to the auto-created Default
83	    # experiment, so "0" would shadow a real row. Keep this in sync with the
84	    # preview script's special-case branch.
85	    uri = mlflow.get_tracking_uri() or "(unset)"
86	    tsv("__hint__", f"⚠ {reason}", uri[:48], detail)
87	
88	
89	def _list_experiments(client: MlflowClient) -> list:
90	    return list(client.search_experiments(max_results=MAX_EXPERIMENTS))
91	
92	
93	def cmd_experiments(client: MlflowClient) -> None:
94	    exps = _list_experiments(client)
95	    if not exps:
96	        tsv("__hint__", "ℹ empty", mlflow.get_tracking_uri()[:48], "No experiments — log a run to see it here")
97	        return
98	    for e in exps:
99	        tsv(
100	            e.experiment_id,
101	            "📊",
102	            e.lifecycle_stage or "-",
103	            e.name or "(unnamed)",
104	            _ms_to_iso(e.last_update_time),
105	        )
106	
107	
108	def _emit_runs(runs: Iterable, exp_name_by_id: dict[str, str]) -> int:
109	    count = 0
110	    for r in runs:
111	        info = r.info
112	        rid = info.run_id
113	        status = STATUS_ICON.get(info.status, info.status or "?")
114	        exp_name = exp_name_by_id.get(info.experiment_id, info.experiment_id)
115	        name = info.run_name or rid[:8]
116	        tsv(rid, status, exp_name, name, _ms_to_iso(info.start_time))
117	        count += 1
118	    return count
119	
120	
121	def cmd_runs_recent(client: MlflowClient) -> None:
122	    exps = _list_experiments(client)
123	    if not exps:
124	        tsv("__hint__", "ℹ empty", mlflow.get_tracking_uri()[:48], "No experiments — log a run to see it here")
125	        return
126	    name_by_id = {e.experiment_id: (e.name or "(unnamed)") for e in exps}
127	    runs = client.search_runs(
128	        experiment_ids=list(name_by_id.keys()),
129	        max_results=MAX_RUNS,

131	    )
132	    if _emit_runs(runs, name_by_id) == 0:
133	        tsv("__hint__", "ℹ empty", mlflow.get_tracking_uri()[:48], "No runs yet — start a run to see it here")
134	
135	
136	def cmd_runs_experiment(client: MlflowClient) -> None:
137	    exp_id = os.environ.get("MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID", "").strip()
138	    if not exp_id:
139	        tsv(
140	            "__hint__",
141	            "ℹ unscoped",
142	            "MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID",
143	            "Press Alt+R on an experiment row, or export MLFLOW_EXPERIMENT_ID=<id> and Ctrl+R",
144	        )
145	        return
146	    try:
147	        exp = client.get_experiment(exp_id)
148	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
149	        _hint("not found", f"experiment_id={exp_id} — {str(e)[:80]}")
150	        return
151	    name_by_id = {exp.experiment_id: (exp.name or "(unnamed)")}
152	    runs = client.search_runs(
153	        experiment_ids=[exp.experiment_id],
154	        max_results=MAX_RUNS,
155	        order_by=["attributes.start_time DESC"],
156	    )
157	    if _emit_runs(runs, name_by_id) == 0:
158	        tsv("__hint__", "ℹ empty", f"exp {exp.experiment_id}", f"No runs in '{exp.name}'")
159	
160	
161	def cmd_models(client: MlflowClient) -> None:
162	    try:
163	        models = list(client.search_registered_models(max_results=200))
164	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001
165	        # Model registry isn't supported by file: backend at all.
166	        _hint("no registry", str(e)[:80])
167	        return
168	    if not models:
169	        tsv("__hint__", "ℹ empty", mlflow.get_tracking_uri()[:48], "No registered models")
170	        return
171	    for m in models:
172	        stages = sorted({v.current_stage for v in (m.latest_versions or []) if v.current_stage})
173	        stage_label = ",".join(stages) if stages else "-"
174	        desc = (m.description or "").splitlines()[0] if m.description else ""
175	        tsv(
176	            m.name,
177	            "📦",
178	            stage_label,
179	            desc or "(no description)",
180	            _ms_to_iso(m.last_updated_timestamp),
181	        )
182	
183

186	        "experiments",
187	        "runs-recent",
188	        "runs-experiment",
189	        "models",
190	    }:

192	            "usage: mlflow-source.py <experiments|runs-recent|runs-experiment|models>",
193	            file=sys.stderr,

195	        return 2

198	    client = MlflowClient()
199

201	    # unreachable HTTP servers and unreadable file/sqlite paths.

204	    except Exception as e:  # noqa: BLE001

1	# Dotfiles Repository — Agent Contract
2	
3	Cross-platform dotfiles managed by **chezmoi** (configs) + **ansible** (system deps). This file is the agent-facing contract: edit rules and cross-file invariants. User-facing intro: [README.md](README.md).
4	
5	> **Headroom rule**: keep this file under ~30k chars. Push handbook content into `docs/`; keep only rules an agent must obey *without* opening another file. `AGENTS.md` and `GEMINI.md` are symlinks to this file — edit one.
6	
7	## Cross-file maintenance rules
8	
9	When you touch one of these surfaces, update the listed mirror in the same commit.
10	
11	| Surface you change | Also update | Reference |
12	|---|---|---|
13	| Config files / ansible roles / platforms / setup steps | `README.md` (What You Get, Supported Platforms, Quick Setup) | — |
14	| New `docs/**/*.md` | Nav entry in `mkdocs.yml`; run `uv run mkdocs build --strict` | known anchor-drift is tracked in [`backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md`](backlog/mkdocs-anchor-drift.md) — don't tighten `validation.links.not_found` until cleared |
15	| New tool installed by an ansible role / Brewfile / curl-installer / mise / uv / npm / cargo / gem / dotnet (or removed, or switched mechanism) | Add / update / remove the row in [`docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md`](docs/this_repo/tool-managers.md) § Tool index (A–Z). If it's a new install **mechanism** (vs new tool through an existing mechanism), also update the relevant § Per-manager catalog subsection and § Decision tree | High-churn case is just the A–Z row (one line per tool). The doc is the install-side companion to [`docs/this_repo/upgrades.md`](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md) — if the new tool has a non-trivial upgrade story, update upgrades.md too. Reverse refs from both pages auto-link back. |
16	| Alias / shell function in `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` | Row in [docs/shells/aliases.md](docs/shells/aliases.md) (name, type, source, scope, one-line) | [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md) for repo-wide config conventions |
17	| Shell history env vars / `setopt`s / atuin filters | Tables in [docs/shells/history.md](docs/shells/history.md) | — |
18	| Linux GUI app in `dot_ansible/roles/gui_apps_linux/` | Inventory table in [docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md](docs/playbooks/linux-gui-apps.md) (the playbook is also the decision tree — read first) | — |
19	| New chezmoi prompt | Edit the `PROMPTS` tuple in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` (the single source of truth: key/kind/default/`prompt_text`/`comment`, plus `condition=When(...)`+`else_value` for host-gated prompts, and `BUNDLES` if applicable), then run `just gen-prompts` to regenerate `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` + `Dockerfile`, and add the key to the README option table. 44	### Workmux status icon integration spans 6 files
45	
46	Touching the `🤖`/`💬`/`✅` per-tmux-window status mechanism requires keeping these 6 surfaces in sync (full story: [docs/tools/workmux.md](docs/tools/workmux.md); pitfall: [pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md](pitfalls/workmux-status-leak.md)):
47	
48	1. `dot_ansible/roles/devtools/tasks/main.yml` — binary install (brew tap on macOS; GitHub release `.tar.gz` on Linux)
49	2. `dot_config/workmux/config.yaml` — `status_format: false` is load-bearing
50	3. `dot_config/tmux/theme.catppuccin.conf` — `#{?@workmux_status, #{@workmux_status},}` appended to `@catppuccin_window_text` and `@catppuccin_window_current_text`
51	4. `dot_claude/modify_settings.json` — `Stop`/`SubagentStop`/`UserPromptSubmit`/`Notification` hooks calling `workmux set-window-status` (hook-aware merger preserves CodeIsland entries)
52	5. `dot_config/opencode/plugins/workmux-status.ts` + `dot_config/opencode/modify_package.json`
53	6. `dot_config/shell/60_tmux_status.sh` — generic POSIX `tmux_status_set/get/clear/clear_all/list/run` for non-agent producers
54	
55	**Hard rules**: never run `workmux setup` on a managed machine (would write parallel hook entries); never flip `status_format: true` (fights catppuccin's window-text override); never drop the `command -v workmux >/dev/null 2>&1 && … || true` guard in Claude hooks (spams errors on fresh boxes); never drop explicit `set-window-status done` from `Stop`/`SubagentStop` (upstream only ever sets `working`, never clears — that's the by-design leak documented in the pitfall). `wt` (worktrunk, `37_worktrunk.zsh`) and `wm` (workmux, `38_workmux.zsh`) stay distinct — different config formats, killer features, helper files.
56

58	
59	This repo uses the `project-knowledge-harness` agent skill (restored on every `chezmoi apply` via `.chezmoiscripts/global/run_onchange_after_40_install_global_skills.sh.tmpl`; see [docs/tools/agent-skills.md](docs/tools/agent-skills.md)). **Load the skill** for the template, disambiguation table, and upgrade path.
60	
61	**Fallback rules** so this section still binds when the skill cannot be loaded:
62	
63	- Three repo-root surfaces, all chezmoi-ignored, all NOT auto-redacted: [`TODO.md`](TODO.md) (priority/effort tags `P1`/`P2`/`P3`/`P?` × `S`/`M`/`L`/`XL`), [`backlog/`](backlog/README.md) (research/design notes for `P?` / `[L]` / `[XL]` / multi-option), [`pitfalls/`](pitfalls/README.md) (debugged traps — **title by symptom, not root cause**, verbatim error messages, never paraphrase).
64	- Capture triggers — future work: "maybe later", "nice to have", "工程量太大需要再評估", "先記下來". Pitfalls: >~15 min debugging, not googleable, non-obvious fix, silent failure.
65	- Do **not** spawn `ROADMAP.md` / `IDEAS.md` / `LESSONS.md` / `TROUBLESHOOTING.md`. Three surfaces, always.
66	- A pitfall *graduates* to a Hard invariant below when it (a) recurs across machines, (b) silently corrupts state, or (c) has a non-obvious workaround. Link back to `pitfalls/<slug>.md`.
67	
68	## Chezmoi templating conventions
69	
70	**Hard rule**: before adding `{{ if eq .profile … }}`, ask if the predicate is auto-detectable. If yes, use `.chezmoi.os` / `.chezmoi.arch` / `.chezmoi.hostname`. `.profile` is for user-role choices only. Values are limited to `macos`, `ubuntu_desktop`, `ubuntu_server` — do **not** introduce new values for OS/arch facts (historical `macos_intel` profile was removed for exactly this reason).
71	
72	**Hard rule — prefer XDG paths.** When a tool supports both a `$HOME`-root dotfile and an XDG path (`~/.config/<tool>/…`), manage the XDG copy (`dot_config/<tool>/…`) to keep `$HOME` tidy; only use a root dotfile when the tool can't read XDG. For tools that error when *both* paths exist (e.g. AeroSpace), also remove the legacy root file via a gated `.chezmoiremove` entry. Full rule + lookup-order caveats: [docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md → A1](docs/this_repo/config-conventions.md).
73	
74	| Predicate | Use |
75	|---|---|
76	| Any macOS | `eq .chezmoi.os "darwin"` |
77	| Any Linux | `eq .chezmoi.os "linux"` |
78	| Apple Silicon | `eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64"` (in darwin scope) or `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "arm64")` |
79	| Intel Mac | `and (eq .chezmoi.os "darwin") (eq .chezmoi.arch "amd64")` |
80	| Desktop vs headless | `.profile` — `ubuntu_desktop` / `ubuntu_server` |
81	
82	Decision table, before/after examples, `macos_intel` migration: [docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-templating.md).
83	
84	## Hard repo invariants
85	
86	### Validate app configs with the app, not just syntax
87	
88	Template rendering / YAML / TOML / JSON syntax is not enough. If the app exposes a config check, parser, dry-run, or debug command, run it against the rendered config before declaring done (e.g. `codex debug …` for `~/.codex/config.toml`; `tmux source-file` / `display-menu` smoke for tmux; `mkdocs build --strict` for docs; for Ansible run the narrowest practical play/tag/check-mode or container smoke — `--syntax-check` alone is a first pass). If a validator cannot be run, say so explicitly in the final report and name the missing command/host/credential.
89	
90	### `primaryShell` choice gates `chsh` only — both shells always deploy
91	
92	`primaryShell` (`zsh` | `bash`, default `zsh`) **only** governs which login shell `chsh` switches to. Both `~/.zshrc`, `~/.bashrc`, `~/.config/{shell,zsh,bash}/` deploy everywhere — users routinely drop into the other shell ad-hoc.
93	
94	**Hard rules**:
95	
96	- Do **not** add `{{ if eq .primaryShell … }}` gates around `dot_zshrc.tmpl`, `dot_bashrc.tmpl`, or `dot_config/{shell,zsh,bash}/**`.
97	- Do **not** gate the zsh / bash ansible roles' **package install** task on `primary_shell` — only `chsh` is gated. macOS bash 5.x brew install + `/etc/shells` whitelist are gated on `primary_shell == "bash"` (zsh-primary mac users skip the brew formula).
98	- Do **not** rely on `$SHELL` — it reflects `/etc/passwd`, lags `chsh` until next login. Use `$ZSH_VERSION` / `$BASH_VERSION`.
99	
100	ble.sh + oh-my-bash 12-step init order in `dot_bashrc.tmpl` is load-bearing: `ble.sh --attach=none` MUST source before bash-preexec/starship; `ble-attach` MUST be the last call before secrets/adhoc; OMB's `autosuggestions` / `syntax-highlighting` / `history-substring-search` plugins MUST be excluded (ble.sh provides natives; double-init causes flicker). Full breakdown: [docs/shells/bash.md](docs/shells/bash.md).
101	
102	### Three-tier user-local override layer
103	
104	User overrides live in **six** untracked files: shared POSIX (`~/.shellrc.adhoc`, `~/.shellrc.secrets`) and per-shell (`~/.zshrc.adhoc`, `~/.bashrc.adhoc`, `~/.config/zsh/secrets.zsh`, `~/.config/bash/secrets.sh`). All six in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`. Default target: shared. Drop to per-shell only when shell-specific syntax is required.
105	
106	**Load order** in both `dot_zshrc.tmpl` and `dot_bashrc.tmpl`:
107	
108	```
109	managed modules → shared secrets → per-shell secrets → shared adhoc → per-shell adhoc
110	```
111	
112	Secrets before adhoc (so adhoc can read secret vars); shared before per-shell (per-shell wins on conflict).
113	
114	**Hard rules**: never add the shared files to chezmoi management; never auto-stub the `*.secrets` files (empty secrets footgun); the shared adhoc stub heredoc lives in BOTH `dot_zshrc.tmpl` AND `dot_bashrc.tmpl` (first shell to run wins; second sees the file and skips) — keep both heredoc bodies in sync. Full matrix: [docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md](docs/shells/adhoc-and-secrets.md).
115	
116	### `enableVimMode` gates shell + tmux vim, NOT Neovim or editors
117	
118	`enableVimMode` (bool, default `true`) gates **shell modal editing + tmux vim navigation only**. Neovim and every editor config (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity/Codex/OpenCode/Cursor-CLI) are **never** affected. Full catalog of the 7 gated templated files + 2 first-seed files (`marimo.toml`, btop's `btop.conf`): [docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md](docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md).
119	
120	**Hard rules**:
121	
122	- Do **not** gate anything under `dot_config/nvim/` — Neovim is inherently vim by design.
123	- Do **not** gate editor configs (`.chezmoitemplates/editor/`, `dot_codex/modify_config.toml.tmpl`, `dot_config/opencode/modify_*.json.tmpl`, `dot_cursor/modify_cli-config.json`) — the flag's semantic is shells + tmux only. Editors want vim → install the editor's vim extension.
124	- Do **not** broaden the gate to `bindkey -M viins`/`vicmd` calls inside `dot_config/zsh/tools/*.zsh` — harmless no-ops without zsh-vi-mode loaded.
125	- The `minimal` bundle in `scripts/init/dotfiles_init.py` forces `enableVimMode = False` (CI/Docker). Don't change without explicit user request.
126	- New vim-touched file → follow the "Yes, gate it" / "No, leave it alone" flow in `docs/this_repo/vim-mode.md` → "For maintainers", and add it to the catalog table in that same page.
127	
128	### Install vs upgrade is split on purpose
129	
130	`chezmoi apply` + ansible is **install-only** (`state: present`, `creates:`). Explicit upgrade path: [`scripts/upgrade_tools.sh`](scripts/upgrade_tools.sh) via `just upgrade-*`. `scripts/**` is in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`, so the upgrade script runs from the repo, never deployed.
131	
132	**Hard rules**:
133	
134	- Do **not** rewrite ansible roles to `state: latest`.
135	- Do **not** add `apt upgrade` / system package bumps to default scope.
136	- **Minimum-version exception**: a role MAY auto-upgrade a single tool inside `chezmoi apply` when it legitimately needs a newer version (e.g. `python_uv_tools` needs `uv >= 0.8.5` for `--with-executables-from`). MUST detect install style (brew vs curl/standalone) and dispatch — never blindly `uv self update` (no-op on brew uv) or `brew upgrade uv` (errors if not a brew formula). Dispatch helper is mirrored in `scripts/upgrade_tools.sh::cat_uv()` and `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/tasks/main.yml`. See [docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md](docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md), [pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md](pitfalls/uv-self-update-homebrew-noop.md), [pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md](pitfalls/ansible-when-regex-replace-backslash-strip.md).
137	- **`with_executables_from:` entries MUST also declare `extra_binaries:`** in `dot_ansible/roles/python_uv_tools/defaults/main.yml`. Without it the install guard short-circuits on hosts where the primary binary already exists, and entry-point shims are never written (silent missing `jupyter` / `jupyter-notebook` despite `jupyter-lab` present). Audit: `yq '.python_uv_tools[] | select(.with_executables_from) | select(.extra_binaries == null) | .name' …` MUST print nothing. See [pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md](pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md).
138	- New upgrade category: [docs/this_repo/upgrades.md → Adding a new category](docs/this_repo/upgrades.md). For a tool already managed by brew/uv/npm/cargo/dotnet/gem/mise: do nothing — generic `upgrade` picks it up.
139	
140	### Sudo session is shared across all run-scripts
141	
142	All three `run_*` scripts share one sudo session via `scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh` — user prompted once at `chezmoi apply` start, reused silently downstream.
143	
144	**Hard rules**:
145	
146	- Do **not** re-implement `sudo -k` / `sudo -v` / TTY-read logic. Call the shared helper.
147	- Do **not** run `sudo -k` (invalidates the cache for the whole flow).
148	- Do **not** register a `trap … EXIT` that removes state (next run-script needs it).
149	- Do **not** read the password into a shell variable. Always `sudo -S <file`.
150	- Do **not** replace `_sudo_spawn_watchdog`'s `setsid`/`nohup` fallback with bare `setsid` — macOS lacks `setsid(1)` in base, the backgrounded failure is silent (redirected to `/dev/null`), and every run-script then re-prompts because `_sudo_state_valid`'s `kill -0` probe finds a dead PID. See [`pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md`](pitfalls/sudo-shared-setsid-macos.md).
151	
152	**Adding a new sudo surface in a run-script**:
153	
154	1. `{{ include "scripts/lib/sudo_shared.sh" }}` near the top of the template.
155	2. Set the `NEED_SUDO` template flag.
156	3. Call `sudo_session_init "yourlabel"`; branch on return code + `sudo_session_skip_reason`.
157	4. Privileged commands via `sudo_run …` or `-e @$CHEZMOI_ANSIBLE_BECOME_FILE` for ansible.
158	
159	**Non-interactive password injection** (used by `scripts/fleet/apply.py` over SSH): `sudo_session_init` adopts `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` (a 0600 file) instead of prompting on `/dev/tty`. **Never** read `CHEZMOI_SUDO_PASSWORD_FILE` directly — always go through `sudo_session_init`. Full API + state + cleanup model: [docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md](docs/this_repo/sudo-session.md).
160	
161	### fleet-apply counter-intuitive defaults
162	
163	Full docs: [`docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md`](docs/this_repo/fleet-apply.md). Load-bearing invariants:
164	
165	- **`drift` ≠ `failed`**. When chezmoi can't prompt to overwrite a hand-edited file (no PTY over SSH), the host shows yellow ⚠ `drift` with paths listed — but it does **not** count toward exit code. Don't auto-"fix" drift unless asked. Resolution: hand-fix the remote, or `--force` to let template win.
166	- **`fleet-apply-file PATH` skips `run_*` scripts** (uses `chezmoi apply --exclude=scripts`). Ansible / Brewfile changes will NOT execute — use full `fleet-apply` for ansible iterations.
167	- **`--branch BRANCH` is no-op on local hosts** (the local source dir IS the user's editor working tree). Local hosts log warn and run against working tree as-is. The flag also forces mode to `apply`.
168	- **Install-only by design** (inherits the previous invariant). `just upgrade-*` must run on each host; fleet-apply does NOT broadcast upgrades.
169	- **Process substitution + sentinel are load-bearing**: `> >(tee -a $log) 2>&1 & _cz_pid=$!; wait $_cz_pid; _rc=$?; echo $_rc > $sentinel`. `--status` / `--tail` / `--watch` + SIGHUP trap depend on `$_cz_pid` pointing to chezmoi, not tee. Don't change to a pipeline.
170	- **Conservative drift classifier**: `_classify_drift()` only downgrades stderr lines matching the exact `chezmoi: <path>: could not open a new TTY: open /dev/tty:` fingerprint. Anything unrecognised stays `failed`. Don't broaden without explicit user request — silent downgrades hide real errors.
171	- **`fleet-status` ≠ `fleet-apply-status`** — easy to confuse:
172	  - `just fleet-status` → **pre-flight readiness probe** (states: `up-to-date`, `behind`, `ahead`, `dirty`, `drift`, `ready-to-update`, `busy`, `init-in-progress`, `toml-mismatch`, `not-init`, `no-source`, `no-chezmoi`, `unreachable`). Run **before** `fleet-apply`. Always exits 0; use `--readiness-json | jq` for scripted gates. `fleet-status-quick` skips remote `git fetch`.
173	  - `just fleet-apply-status` → **process-liveness probe** of `~/.cache/fleet-apply/<host>.{pid,sentinel,log}`. Run **during/after**. Pairs with `fleet-apply-tail` / `fleet-apply-watch` / `fleet-apply-kill`.
174	  - `toml-mismatch` catches a remote's `chezmoi.toml` missing prompt keys that current `.chezmoi.toml.tmpl` requires, via static `_PROMPT_KEY_RE` comparison — `chezmoi dump-config` cannot be used (would re-evaluate the very template we're inspecting).
175	  - `fleet-edit` + `fleet-status` are forgiving (auto-seed / exit 0 with hint); `fleet-apply` keeps strict exit-2 on missing inventory. Don't unify.
176	
177	### `modify_` and `create_` prefix semantics
178	
179	- **`modify_`** files are executable scripts: chezmoi pipes current target contents to stdin, expects new contents on stdout. Used for `~/.claude/settings.json` (jq overlay), editor `settings.json` (VSCode/Cursor/Antigravity), agent CLI configs (`~/.cursor/cli-config.json`, `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`, `~/.codex/config.toml`), `~/.config/herdr/config.toml` (tomlkit overlay — managed tables enforced, herdr's runtime writeback preserved), and `~/.gitconfig` (preserves `[credential "<URL>"]` blocks injected by `gh auth setup-git` so the gh-managed absolute path to the local `gh` binary — different on Intel mac / Apple Silicon / Linuxbrew — survives `chezmoi apply`). **Never** `chezmoi add` a `modify_` target — it would overwrite the script with the live file.
180	- **`create_`** files seed once; chezmoi never touches contents after. Used for `~/.config/nvim/lazy-lock.json` and editor `keybindings.json`. Refresh baseline by copying directly: `cp <target> "$(chezmoi source-path <target>)"`. `chezmoi add` strips the prefix; `chezmoi re-add` silently skips.
181	
182	Case studies + presence-gating in `.chezmoiignore.tmpl`: [docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md](docs/tools/chezmoi-prefixes.md). Three agent CLI overlays (incl. the Claude hook-aware merger that coexists with [CodeIsland](https://github.com/wxtsky/CodeIsland)'s auto-installed hook entries without ping-ponging): [docs/tools/agent-overlays.md](docs/tools/agent-overlays.md).
183	
184	### Tmux popup menu: ≥ 3.3 required + must fit terminal height
185	
186	The popup menu (bound to `prefix + Space` and `prefix + e`) is **generated** by `~/.config/tmux/menu.sh`, not inline in `keybindings.conf`. Two unrelated tmux quirks force this:
187	
188	1. **Position clamping (tmux ≥ 3.3)**: `display-menu -x R -y P` is silently suppressed on tmux 3.2a (Ubuntu 22.04 apt) when it would place the menu past the terminal edge. tmux 3.3+ clamps. `devtools` role auto-upgrades on Debian/Ubuntu (Linuxbrew first, else [`nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage`](https://github.com/nelsonenzo/tmux-appimage) extracted to `~/.local/share/tmux-appimage/` with a `~/.local/bin/tmux` shim). Run `tmux kill-server` once after — running servers keep the old binary in memory.
189	2. **Menu-too-tall silent failure (all versions)**: `display-menu` does **not** paginate. Taller than terminal → entire popup suppressed, no error, nothing in `tmux show-messages`. `man tmux`: _"If the menu is too large to fit on the terminal, it is not displayed."_ Misdiagnosed for hours as a CSI-u keysym bug after a 50-row flat menu started failing on smaller heights.
190	
191	**Hard rules**:
192	
193	- **Top menu cap ≈ 14 rows**. Generator reads `#{client_height}` and tier-trims; retest at heights 14 / 22 / 60 when changing tiers. Push lower-frequency items into category submenus.
194	- **Submenus = separate scripts**, each `exec tmux display-menu …`. Quoting context resets per script.
195	- **Complex commands** (anything with `{`, `}`, `;`, backticks, nested fzf binds) MUST live in their own script. tmux's parser treats `{}` / `;` as command-block delimiters even inside `'…'` inside `"…"`, silently aborting parse.
196	- **Test by shrinking the terminal vertically**. Full-height verification does not catch the height-fit failure.
197	
198	See `pitfalls/tmux-display-menu-silent-fail.md` (red herrings included) and `pitfalls/yazi-tmux-popup-crash.md`.
199	
200	### Key tmux settings for coding agents
201	
202	Non-obvious settings other tools depend on; do not remove without checking:
203	
204	- `extended-keys on` + `terminal-features 'xterm*:extkeys'` — forwards Shift+Enter, Ctrl+Enter, Ctrl+/, Ctrl+digit to inner apps (Claude Code, Neovim, …). **Never use `always`** — re-encodes EVERY `Ctrl+letter` as CSI-u including the LF (Ctrl+J) embedded in pasted multi-line text → ble.sh inserts `^[[106;5u` literally instead of newline. See `pitfalls/tmux-extended-keys-always-paste.md`.
205	- `escape-time 0` — eliminates ESC delay for Neovim.
206	- `set-clipboard on` + `terminal-features …:clipboard` (for `xterm*`, `ghostty*`, `alacritty*`) — OSC 52 over SSH without terminfo `Ms`. Paired with SSH-conditional `vim.g.clipboard = vim.ui.clipboard.osc52` in `dot_config/nvim/lua/config/options.lua`. See [docs/tools/tmux/README.md → OSC 52 Clipboard](docs/tools/tmux/README.md).
207	- `allow-passthrough on` — OSC passthrough for terminal images.
208	- macOS terminals must send Option as Meta/Esc+ for `M-` keybindings (theme switching, layouts, fine resize). Ghostty/cmux: `macos-option-as-alt = left` in `dot_config/ghostty/config`. See [docs/tools/ghostty.md](docs/tools/ghostty.md).
209	
210	Full tmux config breakdown / theme switching / keybindings / troubleshooting: [docs/tools/tmux/](docs/tools/tmux/).
211	
212	### Zellij `default_mode "locked"`
213	
214	`dot_config/zellij/config.kdl` uses `default_mode "locked"` so all keys pass through to inner apps by default. `Ctrl+G` to unlock Zellij commands. First Zellij launch (no existing config): select the "Unlock-First (non-colliding)" keybinding preset.
215

1	# 46_mlf_completion.zsh - tab completion for `mlf` (MLflow umbrella CLI).
2	# Source CLI: dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_mlf (hand-rolled dispatcher) +
3	# scripts/mlf/{plot,list,download}.py (tyro).
4	#
5	# Note: `<run_id>`, `<experiment>`, `<model_name>` are NOT auto-completed
6	# from MLflow because each lookup would round-trip the tracking server (slow,
7	# possibly auth-required). Use `tv mlflow` channel for fuzzy id picking.
8	
9	(( $+commands[mlf] )) || return 0
10	
11	_mlf_list() {
12	    local context state state_descr line
13	    typeset -A opt_args
14	
15	    _arguments -C \
16	        '1: :->kind' \
17	        '*::kind_arg:->kind_args'
18	
19	    case "$state" in
20	        kind)
21	            local -a kinds=(
22	                'experiments:List MLflow experiments'
23	                'runs:List runs (use --experiment to scope)'
24	                'models:List registered models'
25	            )
26	            _describe -t list-kinds 'mlf list kind' kinds
27	            ;;
28	        kind_args)
29	            case "$line[1]" in
30	                runs)
31	                    _arguments \
32	                        '--experiment=[experiment id]:experiment-id:' \
33	                        '--limit=[max rows]:N:' \
34	                        '--json[emit JSON to stdout]'
35	                    ;;
36	                experiments|models)
37	                    _arguments \
38	                        '--limit=[max rows]:N:' \
39	                        '--json[emit JSON to stdout]'
40	                    ;;
41	            esac
42	            ;;
43	    esac
44	}
45	
46	_mlf_plot() {
47	    _arguments \
48	        '1:run-id:' \
49	        '*:metric:' \
50	        '--width=[plot width in chars]:width:' \
51	        '--height=[plot height in chars]:height:' \
52	        '--theme=[plotext theme name]:theme:'
53	}
54	
55	_mlf_download() {
56	    _arguments \
57	        '1:model:' \
58	        '--dest=[output directory]:dir:_directories'
59	}
60	
61	_mlf() {
62	    local context state state_descr line
63	    typeset -A opt_args
64	
65	    _arguments -C \
66	        '1: :->subcommand' \
67	        '*::arg:->args'
68	
69	    case "$state" in
70	        subcommand)
71	            local -a subs=(
72	                'tui:Launch the interactive Textual dashboard (default if no args)'
73	                'tv:Launch tv mlflow fuzzy picker (passes argv + env through)'
74	                'open:Open experiment / run / model page in browser'
75	                'copy:Copy id to clipboard'
76	                'plot:Terminal line plot of metric history'
77	                'list:Tabular dump of experiments / runs / models'
78	                'download:Download a registered model'\''s artifacts'
79	            )
80	            _describe -t subcommands 'mlf subcommand' subs
81	            ;;
82	        args)
83	            case "$line[1]" in
84	                list)     _mlf_list ;;
85	                plot)     _mlf_plot ;;
86	                download) _mlf_download ;;
87	                open|copy) _arguments '1:id:' ;;  # opaque id, can't enumerate
88	                tv)       _arguments '*:tv-arg:' ;;  # passthrough to tv
89	                tui)      ;;  # no args
90	            esac
91	            ;;
92	    esac
93	}

5	#   - binary: executable name to check for idempotency
6	#   - with: (optional) additional dependency to install with --with
7	#   - with_executables_from: (optional) list of packages to install AND
8	#     expose their entry points in ~/.local/bin (e.g. jupyter-core to get
9	#     the `jupyter` meta-CLI; `notebook` to get `jupyter-notebook`)
10	#     NOTE: requires uv >= 0.8.5 (--with-executables-from added in that release)
11	#     For the meta-CLI dispatch model + the 8 jupyter binaries this exposes,
12	#     see docs/tools/notebooks.md "The `jupyter` meta-CLI vs standalone binaries".
13	#     For the auto-upgrade dispatch when uv is too old, see docs/this_repo/uv-bootstrap.md.
14	#   - extra_binaries: (optional) list of additional binary names that must
15	#     also exist in ~/.local/bin for the install to be considered complete.
16	#     Use this whenever `with_executables_from` is set, so adding a new
17	#     entry-point package later triggers a `--force` reinstall on machines
18	#     that already have `binary` present from a prior apply. Without this,
19	#     ansible's `creates:` guard short-circuits the install command and the
20	#     new exec shims are never written. See
21	#     pitfalls/uv-tool-install-creates-guard-misses-executables-from.md.

---

# `yth` — refined design & implementation plan

## 0. Design flaws caught (read these first)

1. **`watch_count` is non-idempotent on re-import.** The proposed `videos.watch_count` + "increment on upsert" breaks the moment you re-run `import-takeout` (every count doubles) or when Takeout and `sync` overlap. Fix: a normalized **`watch_events`** table with `INSERT OR IGNORE`; derive `watch_count/first_watched/last_watched` from it. This makes Takeout re-imports *and* Takeout∩sync overlap idempotent for free. This is the single most important change.
2. **FTS5 external-content needs an INTEGER `content_rowid`.** `videos.video_id` is TEXT, so you cannot use it as `content_rowid`. Add a surrogate `id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` (rowid alias) + `video_id TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL`. Triggers key on `new.id/old.id`.
3. **`platformdirs.user_data_dir("yth")` on macOS returns `~/Library/Application Support/yth/`, not `~/.local/share/yth/`.** The design's stated path is the Linux/XDG value. Either accept the native mac path (matches `sms`/`mi-router` precedent — recommended) or force XDG explicitly. Don't hardcode `~/.local/share`.
4. **`ctrl-b` collides with the tmux prefix (this repo's prefix *is* `Ctrl+b`).** Inside tmux, `C-b` never reaches `tv`; the binding is dead. (`mlflow.toml` mirrors this same latent dead binding.) Use **`alt-b`** to keep the "b-for-browser" mnemonic. CLAUDE.md's keybinding rule explicitly says prefer `Alt+` for new actions.
5. **`yt_dlp` import must stay lazy.** `list`/`show`/`search` use only stdlib `sqlite3` (+ `rich`). Importing `yt_dlp` (~0.3–0.5 s) on the hot `yth show` preview path would make the tv preview pane feel broken. Preview must be **DB-only, zero-network**.
6. **Takeout data is messier than assumed** (see §1.4): localized `"Watched "` title prefix, non-video rows (removed videos, ad/search entries, YouTube Music). Filter and canonicalize.

---

## 1. Module decomposition & DB schema

### 1.1 Module layout (mirrors `scripts/mlf/`)
```
dot_dotfiles/bin/executable_yth        # PEP723 launcher, dict-dispatch, _source_path()
scripts/yth/__init__.py                # shared: db(), connect/migrate, open_id/copy_id,
                                       #   cookie_opts(), url_for(), vtt_to_text(), lazy ytdl()
scripts/yth/import_takeout.py          # tyro Args, def main()->int
scripts/yth/sync.py                    # :ythistory (lazy yt_dlp)
scripts/yth/enrich.py                  # per-video metadata (lazy yt_dlp)
scripts/yth/fetch_subs.py              # subtitle fetch+parse (lazy yt_dlp)
scripts/yth/search.py                  # FTS5 query, rich table / --json
scripts/yth/list.py                    # TSV emitter for the tv source
scripts/yth/show.py                    # DB-only detail (tv preview + `yth show`)
```
`open`/`copy`/`play` are **not** separate modules — like `mlf`, they're thin `_dispatch_*` shims in the launcher calling `open_id/copy_id/play_id` helpers in `__init__.py`. Module filenames use underscores (`import_takeout.py`) while the subcommand is `import-takeout` — the launcher maps `-`→`_`. This matches the repo's Python-module convention and keeps `from scripts.yth.import_takeout import main` importable (a hyphen would be an illegal module name).

DB access (`connect()`, schema `migrate()`, `PRAGMA`s) belongs in `__init__.py` so all eight modules share one code path — same rationale as `make_client()` living in `mlf/__init__.py`.

### 1.2 Schema (concrete)
```sql
PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL;
PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON;

CREATE TABLE videos (
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,          -- rowid alias == FTS content_rowid
  video_id      TEXT UNIQUE NOT NULL,         -- YouTube 11-char id
  title         TEXT,
  channel       TEXT,
  channel_id    TEXT,
  url           TEXT,
  description   TEXT,
  duration      INTEGER,                      -- seconds
  upload_date   TEXT,                         -- 'YYYYMMDD' (yt-dlp native)
  enriched_at   TEXT,                         -- ISO; NULL => needs enrich
  subs_fetched_at TEXT                        -- ISO; NULL => no subs yet
);

-- One row per watch event. Makes every importer idempotent.
CREATE TABLE watch_events (
  video_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  watched_at TEXT NOT NULL,                   -- ISO8601 UTC
  source     TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'takeout', -- 'takeout' | 'sync'
  PRIMARY KEY (video_id, watched_at)          -- de-dupes re-imports
);
CREATE INDEX watch_events_vid ON watch_events(video_id);

CREATE TABLE subtitles (
  id         INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  video_id   TEXT NOT NULL,
  lang       TEXT NOT NULL,
  text       TEXT NOT NULL,
  fetched_at TEXT,
  UNIQUE (video_id, lang)
);

CREATE TABLE meta (key TEXT PRIMARY KEY, value TEXT);  -- sync cursor, last-import ts
```

**Derived watch stats** — compute on read (cheap, indexed) rather than storing denormalized counters:
```sql
CREATE VIEW video_stats AS
SELECT video_id,
       COUNT(*)     AS watch_count,
       MIN(watched_at) AS first_watched,
       MAX(watched_at) AS last_watched
FROM watch_events GROUP BY video_id;
```
Drop `first_watched/last_watched/watch_count` as stored columns on `videos` — they live in the view. (If you later find the view too slow at 100k+ rows, materialize it in an `AFTER INSERT ON watch_events` trigger; not needed initially.)

### 1.3 FTS5 (external-content + triggers — the exact SQL you asked for)
```sql
CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE videos_fts USING fts5(
  title, channel, description,
  content='videos', content_rowid='id',
  tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'
);

CREATE TRIGGER videos_ai AFTER INSERT ON videos BEGIN
  INSERT INTO videos_fts(rowid, title, channel, description)
  VALUES (new.id, new.title, new.channel, new.description);
END;
CREATE TRIGGER videos_ad AFTER DELETE ON videos BEGIN
  INSERT INTO videos_fts(videos_fts, rowid, title, channel, description)
  VALUES ('delete', old.id, old.title, old.channel, old.description);
END;
CREATE TRIGGER videos_au AFTER UPDATE ON videos BEGIN
  INSERT INTO videos_fts(videos_fts, rowid, title, channel, description)
  VALUES ('delete', old.id, old.title, old.channel, old.description);
  INSERT INTO videos_fts(rowid, title, channel, description)
  VALUES (new.id, new.title, new.channel, new.description);
END;

CREATE VIRTUAL TABLE subtitles_fts USING fts5(
  text, content='subtitles', content_rowid='id',
  tokenize='unicode61 remove_diacritics 2'
);
-- analogous ai/ad/au triggers on `subtitles` (single indexed column `text`)
```
This is the canonical external-content pattern (the `'delete'` command-row on UPDATE/DELETE is mandatory — without it the index desyncs). `enrich`'s `UPDATE videos SET description=...` fires `videos_au` and re-indexes automatically, which is exactly why external-content beats a hand-synced standalone table here. For a schema migration you can `INSERT INTO videos_fts(videos_fts) VALUES('rebuild');`.

**Alternative considered & rejected:** a single contentless FTS (`content=''`) over a merged `(video_id UNINDEXED, title, channel, description, subtitle_text)`. Rejected because subtitles are per-lang and large — you'd either denormalize lang rows into the video FTS (awkward) or lose the metadata-only default search that must stay fast. Two external-content tables is cleaner.

### 1.4 Upsert / watch-stat logic (idempotent)
`import-takeout` per row:
```python
vid = extract_id(entry["titleUrl"])            # parse v= / youtu.be; skip if None
if vid is None:                                # removed video / search / ad row
    continue
con.execute("""INSERT INTO videos(video_id,title,channel,channel_id,url)
               VALUES(?,?,?,?,?)
               ON CONFLICT(video_id) DO UPDATE SET
                 title=COALESCE(videos.title, excluded.title),
                 channel=COALESCE(videos.channel, excluded.channel)""",
            (vid, title, channel, channel_id, f"https://youtu.be/{vid}"))
con.execute("INSERT OR IGNORE INTO watch_events(video_id,watched_at,source) VALUES(?,?,?)",
            (vid, iso_utc(entry["time"]), "takeout"))
```
Notes on Takeout reality (verify with your own export):
- `title` is `"Watched <real title>"` (localized — could be `"Regardé"`, `"観た"`). Strip a leading `Watched ` if present, but treat title as provisional; **`enrich` overwrites it with the canonical title** (that's why the ON CONFLICT above only fills NULLs — never clobber an enriched title with the Takeout prefix version). Consider having enrich do an unconditional `SET title=excluded.title`.
- Rows with no `titleUrl`, or `titleUrl` pointing at `google.com/search` / removed-video placeholders → `extract_id` returns None → skipped.
- `channel` = `entry["subtitles"][0]["name"]`; `channel_id` parsed from `subtitles[0]["url"]` (`/channel/UC...`). `subtitles` key absent for some rows — guard.
- `.html` fallback needs `beautifulsoup4`/`lxml` and is fragile (locale-dependent MyActivity markup). **Recommendation: require JSON** (Takeout → "multiple formats" → History = JSON), and defer HTML to backlog rather than shipping a brittle parser in v1.

`sync` (`:ythistory`) has **no per-watch timestamps** — yt-dlp returns ordering only. So sync = "discover newly-watched video_ids": walk newest→oldest, stop at the stored cursor (`meta['sync_cursor']` = newest video_id from last run), `INSERT OR IGNORE` a `watch_events` row with `watched_at = now(), source='sync'`, update the cursor. This is incremental and idempotent; **Takeout stays the source of truth for accurate timestamps.** Document that sync's `last_watched` is approximate.

### 1.5 Search query safety (flaw #8)
Do **not** pass raw user text to `MATCH` — `-`, `:`, `"`, `*`, `(` throw `fts5: syntax error`. Build a safe AND-of-quoted-terms and rank with weighted bm25 (title > channel > description):
```python
fts = " ".join('"' + t.replace('"', '""') + '"' for t in query.split())
cur = con.execute("""
  SELECT v.video_id, v.title, v.channel, s.last_watched
  FROM videos_fts f JOIN videos v ON v.id = f.rowid
  LEFT JOIN video_stats s ON s.video_id = v.video_id
  WHERE videos_fts MATCH ? ORDER BY bm25(videos_fts, 8.0, 4.0, 1.0) LIMIT ?""",
  (fts, limit))
```
`--subs` runs a second query against `subtitles_fts` and UNIONs video_ids (dedupe, tag which matched). Offer a `--raw` flag for power users who want native FTS5 syntax.

---

## 2. yt-dlp LIBRARY recipes

Shared cookie helper in `__init__.py` — the tuple shape is `(BROWSER, PROFILE, KEYRING, CONTAINER)`, only the first is required:
```python
def cookie_opts(cfg) -> dict:
    if cfg.get("cookiefile"):                       # Arc → exported cookies.txt
        return {"cookiefile": os.path.expanduser(cfg["cookiefile"])}
    if cfg.get("from_browser"):                     # e.g. "firefox:/path/to/zen/profile"
        browser, _, profile = cfg["from_browser"].partition(":")
        return {"cookiesfrombrowser": (browser, profile or None, None, None)}
    return {}                                        # public videos need nothing
```

### (a) `:ythistory` flat extraction (cookies required)
```python
opts = {"extract_flat": True, "skip_download": True, "quiet": True,
        "no_warnings": True, **cookie_opts(cfg)}
with ytdl().YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
    info = ydl.extract_info("https://www.youtube.com/feed/history", download=False)
    # ":ythistory" is the alias; the feed URL is equivalent and explicit.
for e in info.get("entries", []):
    vid, title, channel = e["id"], e.get("title"), e.get("uploader") or e.get("channel")
```
`extract_flat=True` avoids a per-video network hit (fast). Flat entries carry `id/title/uploader` and sometimes `duration`; description/upload_date are absent — that's `enrich`'s job.

### (b) Per-video metadata (cookie-free for public)
```python
opts = {"skip_download": True, "quiet": True, "no_warnings": True,
        "extract_flat": False, "sleep_interval": 1, "max_sleep_interval": 3}
with ytdl().YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
    info = ydl.extract_info(f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}", download=False)
```
Column map: `title→title`, `description→description`, `duration→duration` (int secs), `upload_date→upload_date` (`YYYYMMDD`), `channel→channel`, `channel_id→channel_id`. Then `UPDATE videos SET ..., enriched_at=now()` (fires the FTS re-index trigger). Wrap per-video in try/except; on private/removed/age-gated, set `enriched_at=now()` anyway (or a sentinel) so `--limit` batches don't retry the same dead id forever.

### (c) Subtitle text without downloading video (cleanest path)
Let yt-dlp fetch+sign the subtitle URL into a temp dir, then parse the file — more robust than hand-fetching `info['automatic_captions'][lang][*]['url']`:
```python
import tempfile, glob, os
def fetch_subs_for(vid, cfg, langs=("en", "en-US", "en.*")) -> dict[str, str]:
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as td:
        opts = {"skip_download": True, "writesubtitles": True,
                "writeautomaticsub": True, "subtitleslangs": list(langs),
                "subtitlesformat": "vtt", "outtmpl": os.path.join(td, "%(id)s.%(ext)s"),
                "quiet": True, "no_warnings": True,
                "sleep_interval_subtitles": 1,           # throttle bulk
                **cookie_opts(cfg)}
        with ytdl().YoutubeDL(opts) as ydl:
            ydl.download([f"https://www.youtube.com/watch?v={vid}"])
        out = {}
        for path in glob.glob(os.path.join(td, "*.vtt")):
            lang = os.path.basename(path).split(".")[-2]  # <id>.<lang>.vtt
            out[lang] = vtt_to_text(open(path, encoding="utf-8").read())
        return out
```
yt-dlp writes manual subs when present, else auto — no extra logic needed. `subtitleslangs` accepts regex (`"en.*"`). For **public** videos this needs **no cookies**.

VTT → plaintext with rolling-caption dedup:
```python
import re
_TAG = re.compile(r"<[^>]+>")            # <00:00:01.234>, <c>…</c>
def vtt_to_text(vtt: str) -> str:
    out, last = [], None
    for raw in vtt.splitlines():
        line = raw.strip()
        if (not line or line == "WEBVTT" or "-->" in line or line.isdigit()
                or line.startswith(("Kind:", "Language:", "NOTE", "STYLE"))):
            continue
        line = _TAG.sub("", line).strip()
        if line and line != last:        # collapse the auto-caption rolling dup
            out.append(line); last = line
    return " ".join(out)
```
The `line != last` collapse kills the dominant auto-sub artifact (each cue repeats the previous line). If you want near-perfect dedup, request `subtitlesformat="json3"` and concatenate `events[].segs[].utf8` instead — json3 has cleaner segmentation but a fiddlier parser; VTT+dedup is the pragmatic v1 choice.

**Rate-limiting for bulk** (`fetch-subs --all`): process sequentially, set `sleep_interval_subtitles`, add your own `time.sleep(1–2)` between videos, catch `yt_dlp.utils.DownloadError` (esp. HTTP 429) and exponential-backoff. Store `subs_fetched_at` so re-runs skip done videos. Same `sleep_interval/max_sleep_interval` for `enrich`.

`ytdl()` in `__init__.py` is a lazy accessor:
```python
def ytdl():
    import yt_dlp
    return yt_dlp
```
so `search/list/show` never import it.

---

## 3. tv-channel design validation

**Confirmed: television does NOT pass the live query to the source command.** The `[source] command` is a single-shot generator; fuzzy matching happens in-process against the rendered `display` string (exactly how `mlflow.toml` works — multiple fixed sources cycled with `Ctrl+S`, no `{}` query interpolation). Therefore:
- **Subtitle / deep search MUST live in the `yth search --subs` CLI.** The tv channel can only fuzzy-filter the metadata *display string* it was handed. You cannot make `tv yth` search subtitle bodies without pre-loading every subtitle into the display line (absurd).
- **`yth list --tsv` over thousands of rows is fine** as a tv source — television is built for large candidate sets (the `files` channel walks huge trees). Order by `last_watched DESC`. Add a default cap (e.g. `--limit 20000`) with a note; only relevant past ~100k rows.

**Exact TSV layout** (col 0 = id tv hands to preview/actions, mirroring `mlflow-source.py`; all cells `\t`/`\n`-scrubbed via a `_clean()` helper):

| col | content |
|-----|---------|
| 0 | `video_id` (opaque id → preview/actions) |
| 1 | marker: `▶` or `×N` watch-count |
| 2 | channel |
| 3 | title |
| 4 | last_watched `YYYY-MM-DD` |
| 5 | duration `H:MM:SS` |

Channel toml (mirror `mlflow.toml` conventions, `{split:\t:N}`):
```toml
[metadata]
name = "yth"
description = "YouTube watch history: fuzzy-search title/channel; preview metadata + subs"
requirements = ["yth", "uv"]

[source]
command = "yth list --tsv"
# display carries title + channel + date so BOTH are fuzzy-matchable:
display = "{split:\\t:3}  ·  {split:\\t:2}  ({split:\\t:4}, {split:\\t:5}) {split:\\t:1}"
output  = "{split:\\t:0}"                      # Enter/actions receive the video_id
no_sort = true                                 # already ordered last_watched DESC

[preview]
command = "yth show '{split:\\t:0}' | bat --color=always --plain --paging=never --language=markdown"
# yth show is DB-ONLY (no network) so preview stays instant.

[ui]
input_header = "YouTube history"
[ui.preview_panel]
size = 55

[keybindings]
enter  = "actions:open"          # open URL in browser/player
ctrl-y = "actions:copy-url"      # override tv's copy-whole-row default
ctrl-o = "actions:open-browser"  # mlflow precedent (overrides toggle_preview in-channel)
alt-b  = "actions:open-browser"  # "b for browser" mnemonic — alt-b, NOT ctrl-b (tmux prefix!)
alt-p  = "actions:play"          # mpv if present, else browser
alt-s  = "actions:subs"          # fetch-subs then re-show detail
alt-j  = "actions:json"          # yth show --json | bat -l json | less -R
```
Action bodies follow `mlflow.toml`'s pattern: `mode="fork"` for copy/open (fire-and-forget), `mode="execute"` for the pager-based `subs`/`json` (`… | less -R; read -r _`). `copy-url` emits `https://youtu.be/{split:\t:0}` through the same `pbcopy→wl-copy→xclip→OSC52` chain as `mlflow.toml [actions.copy-id]`.

**Mnemonic mirror (o/b/y/p/s/j)** — for a future `yth tui` these become bare letters (`o`=open, `b`=browser, `y`=yank, `p`=play, `s`=subs, `j`=json); record this in the CLAUDE.md cross-file table exactly like the `mlf` row so the two UIs stay in sync.

**Flaw fixed here:** the design's `Ctrl+O/Ctrl+B` — keep `ctrl-o` (works; overrides `toggle_preview` in-channel, precedented) but replace `ctrl-b` with `alt-b`. `Ctrl+b` is this repo's tmux prefix and is swallowed before `tv` ever sees it.

---

## 4. Cookie strategy (end-to-end)

- **Public videos (the common case): no cookies.** `enrich` and `fetch-subs` of public videos need nothing — `cookie_opts()` returns `{}`. Only age-restricted / members-only / private / your-own-unlisted need cookies. Correct as designed.
- **`sync` (`:ythistory`) always needs login cookies** (it's your account's feed).
- **Zen (Firefox fork): auto-detect + `firefox:<profile-path>`.** Glob `~/Library/Application Support/zen/Profiles/*/cookies.sqlite` (or read `profiles.ini` for the Default), then `cookiesfrombrowser=("firefox", <profile_dir>, None, None)`. yt-dlp's `firefox` keyword reads the Firefox cookie format Zen uses; passing the explicit profile path is what makes it work despite Zen not being a recognized browser keyword. Config: `from_browser = "firefox:/Users/david/Library/Application Support/zen/Profiles/xxxx.Default"`. (Zen isn't installed on this host — auto-detect must degrade gracefully to "no cookie source configured".)
- **Arc (Chromium fork): cookies.txt fallback.** yt-dlp's `chrome` keyword derives the Keychain service name as *"Chrome Safe Storage"*; Arc's is *"Arc Safe Storage"* and there's **no yt-dlp flag to override the service name** (the `+KEYRING` suffix is Linux-only: kwallet/gnome/basictext). So `--cookies-from-browser chrome` cannot decrypt Arc. Concrete export method: install the **"Get cookies.txt LOCALLY"** extension (MV3, offline, Chrome Web Store — installs in Arc since Arc is Chromium), visit youtube.com logged in, Export → save as e.g. `~/.config/yth/cookies.txt`, then set `cookiefile = "~/.config/yth/cookies.txt"` in `config.toml`. Document that these expire and need periodic re-export. (This only matters for `sync`; enrich/fetch-subs of public videos never hit it.)
- Nothing above is wrong in the design; the only correction is **naming the concrete Arc export tool** and the reason `chrome` keyword fails.

**Config `~/.config/yth/config.toml` (via `user_config_dir`)** — mutually-exclusive cookie source, plus:
```toml
# cookies (optional; only sync + restricted videos need them)
cookiefile   = "~/.config/yth/cookies.txt"          # Arc path
# from_browser = "firefox:/…/zen/Profiles/xxxx.Default"  # Zen path (auto-detected if unset)
langs        = ["en", "en-US"]
open_target  = "browser"                            # browser | mpv
```
